title: Tokyo in 5 Days — Shibuya, Odaiba, Disney, Asakusa
subtitle: Shibuya, Odaiba, Disney and Asakusa: the classic five days for a first visit to Tokyo
summary: Five days of Tokyo from a full travelogue: Shibuya and Harajuku, Odaiba, Tokyo Disney, Asakusa and Skytree are all in. The Gundam factory and the Unicorn Gundam are gone, so teamLab Planets takes their place. Kameari, Akihabara, DiverCity and Shiba Park are kept as alternates. The notes cover entry, transit cards and reservations.

Changed since the travelogue
GUNDAM FACTORY YOKOHAMA closed in March 2024, so the original stop is replaced by teamLab Planets and the Odaiba area.

The life-size Unicorn Gundam statue in Odaiba ended its display on 31 Aug 2026 (announced by the operator, TOKYO GUNDAM PROJECT; report https://dengekionline.com/article/202608/85200 , checked 2026-11-17), so it is not included.
The National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) is under renovation (the official site says it reopens on 23 Apr 2027), so it is not included.
Could not be confirmed from official sources; check before you go
SHIBUYA SKY hours and reservation rules (the official page could not be retrieved).
Tokyo DisneySea's hours for the day and the night show (the official site timed out).
teamLab Planets hours (the official page could not be retrieved, and third-party sources contradict each other).
Hours for the Fuji TV spherical observatory, the National Diet Building's visitor rules, LE LABO, Kiwamiya and the restaurants.
Fares and journey times of the Narita Express and the Asakusa Line Airport Rapid (the official sites would not open; the 2023 travelogue's figures are used).
Travelogue details
The hotel follows the author's trip in June 2023: Shiodome, four nights in a row.
The travelogue's Kochikame stop in Kameari and Akihabara are not in the daily plans (see the alternates).
Entry and internet
Before you leave, register your immigration and customs declaration on Visit Japan Web: https://www.vjw.digital.go.jp/main/#/vjwpco001
For data, use a physical SIM or an eSIM.
Getting around

Trains, subways and buses take Suica or PASMO; on an iPhone you can add Suica to Wallet. The travelogue's author used the Suica on an iPhone in 2023; Android users can buy a Welcome Suica at Narita Airport.

Airport to the city: every seat on the Narita Express (成田エクスプレス) is reserved, and tapping a transit card at the gate will be refused, so buy a reserved-seat ticket first (from the travelogue; see the JR East website for details).
Shiodome Station exits straight onto the Yurikamome and the Oedo Line; for other districts it is about a 10-minute walk to Shimbashi Station (JR, the Ginza Line and the Asakusa Line).

Back to Narita: from Shimbashi the Toei Asakusa Line Airport Rapid runs direct in about 1 hour 15 min; the travelogue says that ticket could not be paid for by card or Suica at the time, so carry plenty of cash.
On Tokyo buses you tap your card when you board (unlike Kyoto, where you pay when you get off).
Reservations
Book SHIBUYA SKY, Tokyo DisneySea, teamLab Planets and Tokyo Skytree early and reserve time slots; popular dates are usually gone on the day.
The DisneySea entrance is past the in-park train; the travelogue's author bought a DisneySea one-park ticket, so no castle and no parade; front-row seats for the night water show are sold separately.
Observation decks and Disney hours differ every day, so check the official sites before you go.
Other

Carry plenty of yen in cash: drugstores, the airport express ticket and some other places turned out not to take cards, or the card was refused; the travelogue suggests keeping at least ¥10,000 on you.
The duty-free and tax-refund rules have changed in recent years; check the Japan Tourism Agency's explanation before you leave.
You can leave bags at the hotel; on the last day the travelogue's author left them there and then shopped without them.
Restaurants inside the Disney parks are often full, so the travelogue suggests bringing a snack.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 5 days run
paragraphs: In and out of Narita, with one hotel in Shiodome as the base for all four nights, so you never repack. Every day starts from Shiodome by train, and you can leave your bags at the hotel on the first and last days to sightsee light.
Day 1: land at Narita, drop your bags in Shiodome, then head to Shibuya at dusk for {@d1-03}, a Kobe beef steak and hamburg dinner, and the view from {@d1-05}.
Day 2: start at {@d2-01}, then Odaiba for the Statue of Liberty, takoyaki and the Fuji TV building; in the afternoon Shinjuku for department stores and drugstores, and an izakaya dinner.
Day 3: the whole day at Tokyo DisneySea, with Toy Story Mania and Soaring in the morning, Journey to the Center of the Earth and Indiana Jones in the afternoon, and the {@d3-04} to end the night.
Day 4: begin at {@d4-01}, then Meiji Jingu, lunch around Harajuku and Omotesando and a stop at LE LABO; in the afternoon {@d4-05} in Asakusa, dinner at Solamachi, and the view from {@d4-07}.

Day 5: check out and leave your bags, see the {@d5-02} and the Imperial Palace East Gardens in the morning, tempura soba for lunch at Tokyo Station, a photo of the {@d5-05}, then pick up your bags and head to Narita.
Where to sleep: Hotel Villa Fontaine Grand Tokyo-Shiodome for all four nights, one base from start to finish; Shiodome Station has the Yurikamome and the Oedo Line right at the exit.

Getting around: trains, subways and buses take Suica or PASMO; the Narita Express is all reserved seats, so buy a reserved-seat ticket first; on the way back, the Toei Asakusa Line airport rapid from Shimbashi runs direct in about 1 hour 15 minutes, and that fare could not be paid by card or Suica at the time, so carry enough cash. Reaching other districts from Shiodome means about a 10-minute walk to Shimbashi Station. Check the latest timetables before you go.
Who it suits: first-timers, or anyone who wants Tokyo's classics in one trip. It includes a full day at Disney, so bring the energy; book SHIBUYA SKY, DisneySea, teamLab Planets and Skytree early.
